context: Tests whether the agent applies this tile's prescribed release sequencing and version-bump policy. The tile prescribes: patch bumps are delegated to the CI pipeline (`tesslio/patch-version-publish` auto-bumps the patch segment on every merge) so manual manifest edits for patch changes are wrong; minor and major bumps require manual manifest updates to specific target numbers; breaking changes need explicit impact surfacing in the runbook; PRs should be sequenced patch → minor → major for risk management. Baseline agents typically bump all three manually and do not sequence the releases.

checklist.name: Patch: no manual manifest update
checklist.description: For the bug-fix change (null-pointer guard, backward-compat, no API change), the runbook does NOT prescribe a manual manifest version bump. Baseline agents will typically bump it manually; the tile prescribes delegating to CI

checklist.name: Patch: explains CI auto-bump
checklist.description: The runbook explains WHY the patch case skips a manual bump — because the CI pipeline (`tesslio/patch-version-publish` or equivalent) auto-bumps the patch segment on every merge. Mentioning the specific automation or its role is tile-prescribed knowledge; a baseline agent without the tile would not know this wiring exists

checklist.name: Minor: manifest bumped to `1.5.0`
checklist.description: For the CSV-export change (additive new route, backward-compat), the runbook updates the manifest version to `1.5.0` (not `1.4.3`, not `2.0.0`). Scores correct classification (minor) AND correct arithmetic

checklist.name: Major: manifest bumped to `2.0.0`
checklist.description: For the v1-routes removal (breaking change), the runbook updates the manifest version to `2.0.0` (not `1.4.3`, not `1.5.0`). Scores correct classification (major) AND correct arithmetic

checklist.name: Major: flags breaking-change impact for downstream
checklist.description: The runbook calls out that the v1-routes removal will break existing clients AND surfaces migration guidance in a place a downstream consumer would see (release notes, migration guide, or a deployment checklist). An agent who treats the major bump the same way as the minor bump — no impact statement, no migration — scores zero

checklist.name: Release sequencing: patch first, major last
checklist.description: The runbook orders the three PRs patch → minor → major with explicit rationale (patch is low-risk and gets CI's auto-bump first; major gives downstream the longest notice and comes last). Any coherent risk-based sequencing with stated reasoning passes; no sequencing, or reversing without justification, scores zero. Baseline agents typically do not sequence

checklist.name: Readiness gate: tests + linter
checklist.description: The runbook requires tests AND linter to pass before creating any of the three PRs. Scored once as a cross-cutting gate, not duplicated per change

checklist.name: Runbook covers all three changes separately
checklist.description: The `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md` has a distinct section for each of the three pending changes, each answering the readiness / versioning / sequencing questions in the task's output spec. A single conflated section scores zero

checklist.name: PR titles follow conventional-commits format
checklist.description: The runbook prescribes PR titles in the `<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>` form for each change (conventional commits — widely adopted public convention). A baseline agent familiar with conventional commits will likely produce this, but the runbook should explicitly call it out as the team's chosen style
